newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber market ends week down.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber market ends week down.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower as the market completed another week with minimal participation from buyers, traders said.

"I don't think there's any point in watching the market at all next week," said a trader, referring to the oncoming Christmas and New Year festivities which had already distracted players since the start of December.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for January RSS1 buyer at 316.50 cents ($1.25) a kg, down two cents from Thursday. January SMR 20 buyer was half cent lower at 308.
Trading houses were quoting the SMR 20 at 309/310 cents, SMR CV at 367, SMR L at 348, SMR 10 at 312, and drum latex at 240.
"Producers also want to take it easy until the New Year," said another trader. "If they're going to sell now, there has to be a good premium.
Dealers said rains since last month have reduced supply of latex and other raw materials into the market.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 243.22 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 19 from 242.78 on Dec 18. The daily indicator price fell to 243.18 from 243.30.
